edges.reason: E2E closure verifies the 429 decision is honored in the shipped retry behavior (gate E1) and that the verification document matches observed call counts
E2E closure exercises the retry loop against the real provider/store seams (gates E1, E2, E3)

unlock_contracts.rationale: T01 verifies the assumption behind frozen C1 while running in parallel with C1's owner T02; C1's unfreeze_rule handles the FALSIFIED case as a replan gate, not an execution edge
T01 reads the frozen provider interface C3 (docstring + capture test) while its owner T02 runs in parallel

contract_bindings.rationale: the retry policy is implemented in app/notify.py, which T02 owns; T01 consumes C1's unfreeze_rule to verify the 429 assumption behind it; T03 verifies the policy end to end (E1)
app/db.py is modified by no task; the record shape is finalized by the service writer (T02) and verified end to end by T03 (E2)
the ProviderClient interface (app/provider.py) is pre-existing and frozen — no task modifies it; T02's retry wrapper is the concrete owner of its usage semantics; T03 counts its calls (E1)

seam_bindings.rationale: S1's logical participants 'service' and 'provider-client' bind to T02 (retry wrap in the service) and T01 (provider-boundary verification via the staging-capture test)
S2's logical participants 'service' and 'persistence' bind to T02 (record writer) and T03 (e2e closure, which reads the record back to verify one-record-per-call)

fake_serialization_removed.why_not_real: naive 'verify then implement' ordering rejected: C1 (retry policy incl. retry-on-429) and C3 (provider interface) are frozen, so T02 implements against the frozen spec with test fakes; T01's FALSIFIED verdict triggers C1's unfreeze_rule (request_contract_revision) — a plan-validity gate, not an execution edge. Ordering them would serialize 2 of 3 tasks for no data dependency.

collisions_handled: none — owned paths are disjoint by construction (T01: docs/ only; T02: app/notify.py + tests/test_retry.py; T03: tests/test_e2e_retry.py)
